articles.title: Who Is Ashoke Sen? The Kolkata Physicist Who Unified String Theory — and Just Became the First Indian to Win the Oskar Klein Medal
articles.excerpt: He did his apprenticeship at Fermilab and Stanford, then chose in 1988 to build his career in India. Four decades later, Ashoke Sen — Breakthrough Prize laureate, Dirac medallist, Fellow of the Royal Society at 42 — has received Stockholm's Oskar Klein Medal, an honour no Indian physicist had won in its 38 years.
articles.image_caption: Theoretical physicist Ashoke Sen in the Physics department of Scottish Church College, Kolkata, in 2019. Sen received the 2026 Oskar Klein Medal in Stockholm, becoming the first Indian physicist to win the honour.

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.excerpt: A memo from Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to Secretary of State Marco Rubio says Iran has substantially increased efforts to target US personnel, prompting embassy staff reductions across the Middle East.
articles.nri_angle: Embassy drawdowns in Gulf states hosting large Indian communities raise the regional risk backdrop for diaspora families with relatives working in the Middle East.

articles.title: Gangster Himanshu Bhau Arrested in Las Vegas After Indian Tip-Off
articles.excerpt: Tracked by Delhi and Haryana police teams and shared with US law enforcement, the red-notice fugitive was arrested Thursday evening alongside Neeraj Faridpuria; Indian agencies are now pushing to expedite his deportation.
articles.image_caption: Himanshu Bhau in a file photograph circulated by Indian media. The Haryana gangster, wanted in more than 30 cases, was arrested in Las Vegas on Thursday after Indian agencies shared his tracked location with US law enforcement.
articles.nri_angle: The arrest shows Indian agencies tracking a fugitive who ran extortion rackets back home from North America, a pattern that has put gang migration routes under scrutiny in both countries.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: Interpol red notice issued against Himanshu Bhau.
Bhau obtained a passport using forged papers.

articles.title: US Quietly Pulls Diplomats' Families From Gulf Posts as Houthi Attacks Escalate
articles.excerpt: Saudi Arabia gets a formal ordered departure while Lebanon, the UAE, Qatar and Jordan quietly trim staffing — leaving families who only just returned facing a second uprooting in a year.
articles.image_caption: The Harry S Truman Building, headquarters of the US Department of State in Washington. The US has ordered non-emergency staff and families out of Saudi Arabia and trimmed staffing at regional embassies.
articles.nri_angle: Millions of Indians live and work in the Gulf states covered by the drawdown, and US embassy staffing cuts are an early public signal of how Washington rates the escalation risk around them.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Milan Condemn Racist Abuse of Maignan After Bournemouth Red Card
articles.excerpt: AC Milan said goalkeeper and captain Mike Maignan faced serious and unacceptable racist abuse on social media after his 27th-minute sending-off in the 3-0 Europa League defeat at Bournemouth.
articles.image_caption: AC Milan goalkeeper Mike Maignan, in the pink goalkeeper kit with number 16, stands on the right as Bournemouth players gather around Tyler Adams on the ground at Bournemouth. Maignan was sent off in the 27th minute of the Europa League match, and Milan later condemned racist abuse directed at him on social media.
articles.nri_angle: A global football racism case involving a leading Black goalkeeper, relevant to diaspora readers who follow European football and face discrimination debates in sport.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.nri_angle: For Indian-American and other voters, the case is a test of how far a federal court will go to intervene in a state-run Senate election before certification.
